items.title: John Batiste "Bat" Mosley Interview, 1961-09-23
items.q: The interviewee mentions 'Buddy Johnson and Yank Johnson' as bands that 'played those Jitney dances' and 'worked mostly in Yawlin', but does not state that he personally played with, met, or was in a group with Buddy Johnson.

ctx.x: He could play too. Are there any of the other old time bands here that you can remember? For instance, they tell me about the Johnson brothers, Yank and the other. Yank, yeah. Yeah, it was Yank. There were two brothers. Both of them playing tram along. Buddy.

Buddy Johnson and Yank Johnson. And Frankie Dusen was over on the side. Frankie Dusen, yeah. Did you know that when they lived over here? I guess I did. He was playing tram along too. Yeah. He was a barber. He used to cut my hair. See where the Catholic cemetery right there? Yeah. That's the Catholic cemetery right opposite the Catholic cemetery. They were staying there. That's where the old man and all used to stay. Frankie Dusen, they call him. Frankie Dusen, his dad and all. You know his daddy played any…
That was the man that the fast told us about. Cheese. Some joke about cheese. Yeah, he's fantastic.

ctx.x: Well, Bill was playing. That's the first sister we picked up. Drum. Yeah, he picked up drum. He used to play with a, oh, I forget the name of the band. I know the fellow who used to play trumpet. He was dead now. He was dead now. Lego. Lego? Lego, yeah. He was a good trumpet player too. That was old time. He had a beautiful tone.
